Backcast of the raw series

Source: R/forecast.R
backcast.Rd

Backcasts the raw series, i.e. predicts the periods preceding its start, from the pre-adjustment model of a model fitted with X13(), TRAMOSEATS(), REGARIMA() or TRAMO(). fabletools has no backcast generic, so this function plays the role of forecast() for the past. The distribution is built as for forecasts (log-normal for log-transformed series, normal otherwise; see the Distribution section of forecast.jd3_model).

Usage

backcast(object, h, ...)

# S3 method for class 'jd3_model'
backcast(object, h, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mdl_ts'
backcast(object, h, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mdl_df'
backcast(object, h, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted jd3_model (usually a column of a mable).

h

Number of periods to backcast, immediately before the start of the series.

...

Other arguments passed by forecast() (e.g. times), ignored.

Value

For a jd3_model or a mdl_ts, a tsibble with the h dates preceding the series and a distribution column dist (see distributional). For a mable, a tibble with the key columns, .model, the dates and dist, one block per model. Use mean() or median() on dist to get a point backcast; the median equals JDemetra+'s backcast.

See also

forecast.jd3_model, jd3_indicator() for the raw indicators (y_b, y_eb...).

Examples

y  <- tsibble::as_tsibble(AirPassengers)
mb <- model(y, x13 = X13(value))

bc <- backcast(mb, h = 12)
bc
#> # A tibble: 12 × 3
#>    .model    index
#>    <chr>     <mth>
#>  1 x13    1948 Jan
#>  2 x13    1948 Feb
#>  3 x13    1948 Mar
#>  4 x13    1948 Apr
#>  5 x13    1948 May
#>  6 x13    1948 Jun
#>  7 x13    1948 Jul
#>  8 x13    1948 Aug
#>  9 x13    1948 Sep
#> 10 x13    1948 Oct
#> 11 x13    1948 Nov
#> 12 x13    1948 Dec
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: dist <dist>

# A single model
bc1 <- backcast(mb$x13[[1]], h = 12)
median(bc1$dist)
#>  [1] 102.01134 109.21372 122.48921 115.92638 109.30768 127.82206 138.17197
#>  [8] 138.91709 130.22180 108.52204  96.88531 113.92835
